cases.name: can-id-above-arbitration-field
cases.desc: An identifier of 0x3FFFFFFF. MUST be refused, not masked: masking silently produced 0x1FFFFFFF, a frame the caller never asked for, on the field a client uses to decide what the payload means. The format is carried by `extended`, not by high bits of `id`.

cases.name: can-id-negative
cases.desc: An identifier of -1. Masking turned it into 0x1FFFFFFF -- the same frame an over-large identifier became, so two different mistakes produced one wrong answer.

cases.name: can-first-record-dt-nonzero
cases.desc: SPEC.md 6.1 -- t_base IS record 0's arrival time.

cases.name: can-classic-nine-bytes
cases.desc: SPEC.md 6.10 -- a Classic frame carries 0..8.

cases.name: can-len-longer-than-payload
cases.desc: SPEC.md 6 -- len 8 with one byte of payload. Padding to eight publishes seven bytes the caller never supplied, on a bus signal a client will decode as a measurement.

cases.name: can-len-shorter-than-payload
cases.desc: SPEC.md 6 -- len 0 with one byte of payload. Discarding it silently drops data the caller asked to send.

cases.name: gps-latitude-beyond-the-pole
cases.desc: SPEC.md 5.4 -- a latitude of 91 degrees, with the position bit set so the range rule applies.

cases.name: gps-rtk-float-and-fixed
cases.desc: SPEC.md 5.3 -- the two RTK bits are exclusive.

cases.name: gps-rtk-without-differential
cases.desc: SPEC.md 5.3 -- an RTK solution is a differentially corrected one, so the bit is implied and not optional.

cases.name: gps-ext-count-disagrees
cases.desc: SPEC.md 5.5 -- three extensions declared, none supplied.

cases.name: imu-period-zero
cases.desc: SPEC.md 7 -- zero says every sample was taken at one instant.

cases.name: can-empty-batch
cases.desc: SPEC.md 6.2 -- t_base names record 0, so a batch with no records timestamps a frame that does not exist.

cases.name: imu-empty-batch
cases.desc: SPEC.md 7 -- t_base names sample 0, so a batch with no samples timestamps one that does not exist.

cases.name: monitor-declaration-repeats-a-slot
cases.desc: SPEC.md 13.3 -- the decoder already rejected this, so an encoder emitting it produced a declaration its own reader refuses.

cases.name: monitor-channel-with-no-deadline
cases.desc: SPEC.md 13.5 -- every declared channel carries a deadline. A channel with none is a value a device can go on displaying forever after the client stopped sending it.

cases.name: monitor-asks-for-more-than-fits
cases.desc: SPEC.md 13.4 -- more channels than fit in one complete write.

cases.name: monitor-update-with-no-values
cases.desc: SPEC.md 13.4 -- an empty write is not a complete statement of what the client can supply.

cases.name: monitor-update-repeats-a-slot
cases.desc: SPEC.md 13.4 -- nothing says which of the two wins.

cases.name: control-detail-on-a-refusal
cases.desc: SPEC.md 9 -- detail is present if and only if status is ok.

cases.name: time-sync-answered-before-asked
cases.desc: SPEC.md 9.7 -- a negative round trip halved into an offset is a confidently wrong clock.

cases.name: can-ordinary-batch
cases.desc: A frame at the top of the arbitration field, which is legal.

cases.name: monitor-well-formed-declaration
cases.desc: Distinct slots, inside the channel cap.

cases.name: imu-ordinary-batch
cases.desc: Accel and gyro both present, a non-zero period, two samples.

cases.name: time-sync-simultaneous
cases.desc: SPEC.md 9.7 -- t_device_tx MUST NOT be EARLIER than t_device_rx, so equal readings are legal. A device whose clock cannot resolve the two instants apart reports them equal rather than inventing a gap.

cases.name: info-can-without-control
cases.desc: SPEC.md 4.1 -- `can` requires `control`. A device that publishes this has advertised a role no client can use, because CAN_SUBSCRIBE is the only way to install one.

cases.name: info-capacity-without-capability
cases.desc: SPEC.md 4.1 -- every CAN capacity is zero while the `can` bit is clear. Masking the capacity instead would publish a different device from the one the caller described.

cases.name: reserved-bits-info-capabilities
cases.desc: SPEC.md 2 -- info.capabilities bits 9-31 are reserved in VTP/1.0, so an encoder MUST zero them rather than publish a meaning this version has not assigned. Bit 31 is set because an encoder masking at the wrong width passes on the lowest reserved bit and fails on the highest.

cases.name: reserved-bits-info-clock-flags
cases.desc: SPEC.md 2 -- info.clock_flags bits 2-7 are reserved in VTP/1.0, so an encoder MUST zero them rather than publish a meaning this version has not assigned. Bit 7 is set because an encoder masking at the wrong width passes on the lowest reserved bit and fails on the highest.

cases.name: reserved-bits-gps-fix-validity
cases.desc: SPEC.md 2 -- gps_fix.validity bits 12-31 are reserved in VTP/1.0, so an encoder MUST zero them rather than publish a meaning this version has not assigned. Bit 31 is set because an encoder masking at the wrong width passes on the lowest reserved bit and fails on the highest.

cases.name: reserved-bits-gps-fix-fix-flags
cases.desc: SPEC.md 2 -- gps_fix.fix_flags bits 5-7 are reserved in VTP/1.0, so an encoder MUST zero them rather than publish a meaning this version has not assigned. Bit 7 is set because an encoder masking at the wrong width passes on the lowest reserved bit and fails on the highest.

cases.name: reserved-bits-can-header-flags
cases.desc: SPEC.md 2 -- can_header.flags bits 1-7 are reserved in VTP/1.0, so an encoder MUST zero them rather than publish a meaning this version has not assigned. Bit 7 is set because an encoder masking at the wrong width passes on the lowest reserved bit and fails on the highest.

cases.name: reserved-bits-imu-header-flags
cases.desc: SPEC.md 2 -- imu_header.flags bits 3-7 are reserved in VTP/1.0, so an encoder MUST zero them rather than publish a meaning this version has not assigned. Bit 7 is set because an encoder masking at the wrong width passes on the lowest reserved bit and fails on the highest.

cases.name: reserved-bits-monitor-value-validity
cases.desc: SPEC.md 2 -- monitor_value.validity bits 1-7 are reserved in VTP/1.0, so an encoder MUST zero them rather than publish a meaning this version has not assigned. Bit 7 is set because an encoder masking at the wrong width passes on the lowest reserved bit and fails on the highest.

cases.name: reserved-bits-link-params-validity
cases.desc: SPEC.md 2 -- link_params.validity bits 4-15 are reserved in VTP/1.0, so an encoder MUST zero them rather than publish a meaning this version has not assigned. Bit 15 is set because an encoder masking at the wrong width passes on the lowest reserved bit and fails on the highest.

cases.name: reserved-bits-power-state-validity
cases.desc: SPEC.md 2 -- power_state.validity bits 2-7 are reserved in VTP/1.0, so an encoder MUST zero them rather than publish a meaning this version has not assigned. Bit 7 is set because an encoder masking at the wrong width passes on the lowest reserved bit and fails on the highest.

cases.name: control-detail-on-ok
cases.desc: SPEC.md 9 -- detail accompanies `ok`, and only `ok`. The refusal case above is only half the rule.
